cases.sentence: Пойдешь направо – обязательно попадешь на Курский ___.
cases.translation: If you turn right, you are bound to end up at the Kursk railway station.
cases.explain: «На» with a verb of motion («попадешь») answers «куда?» and takes the accusative; вокзал is inanimate, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.sentence: Скучно тебе было в этих ___, Веничка.
cases.translation: You were bored in those back lanes, Venichka.
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (location, not direction) requires the prepositional case, here in the plural: в проулках.

cases.sentence: Захотел ты ___ – вот и получай свою суету.
cases.translation: You wanted bustle — well then, take your bustle.
cases.explain: The verb «захотеть» takes the genitive when the thing wanted is abstract or indefinite: захотел суеты.

cases.sentence: Я лучше прислонюсь к ___ и зажмурюсь.
cases.translation: I would rather lean against a column and screw my eyes shut.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (towards, up against) always governs the dative: к колонне.

cases.translation: In half an hour the shop will open.
cases.explain: The word is the subject of the verb «откроется», and subjects stand in the nominative.

cases.translation: You should drop into the station restaurant.
cases.explain: «В» with motion into a place («зайди») takes the accusative; the inanimate ресторан keeps the nominative-looking form.

cases.sentence: Не ехать же в Петушки без ___.
cases.translation: One really cannot travel to Petushki without presents.
cases.explain: The preposition «без» always governs the genitive, here the genitive plural: без гостинцев.

cases.translation: Between the first and the second glass of hunter's vodka?
cases.explain: «Между» in the sense of 'between' governs the instrumental, so стакан becomes стаканом.

reading.ru: Ну вот, я же знал, что говорил: пойдешь направо – обязательно попадешь на Курский вокзал.
reading.question: Where does Venichka find himself at the start of the chapter?
options: On the square in front of the Kursk railway station
In the entrance hall where he woke up
reading.correct: On the square in front of the Kursk railway station
reading.explain: He notes that his own rule has come true again: turn right and you inevitably land at the Kursk station.

reading.ru: Скучно тебе было в этих проулках, Веничка, захотел ты суеты – вот и получай свою суету…
reading.question: How does Venichka explain to himself why he has ended up in the crowd?
options: He was bored in the back lanes and wanted bustle
He was following the angels' orders
He was looking for his suitcase
He wanted to see the Kremlin one more time
reading.correct: He was bored in the back lanes and wanted bustle
reading.explain: He reproaches himself for being bored in the side streets and asking for the bustle he now has.

reading.ru: Ведь вот Искупитель даже, и даже Маме своей родной, и то говорил: «Что мне до тебя?»
reading.question: Whom does Venichka quote to justify not caring about the people around him?
options: The Redeemer, who said even to his own Mother "What is that to me?"
An acquaintance who drank coriander vodka
The angels, who told him to ignore the crowd
A fellow passenger on the train to Petushki
reading.correct: The Redeemer, who said even to his own Mother "What is that to me?"
reading.explain: He cites the Redeemer's words to his own Mother as licence to care nothing for the fussing, tiresome people.

reading.ru: Я лучше прислонюсь к колонне и зажмурюсь, чтобы не так тошнило…
reading.question: What does Venichka decide to do to make the nausea easier to bear?
options: Lean against a column and shut his eyes
reading.correct: Lean against a column and shut his eyes
reading.explain: He leans on a column and screws his eyes shut, and the voice from above approves.

reading.question: Who speaks to Venichka in a soft, tender voice from above?
reading.explain: He recognises the voice at once as the angels of the Lord, who have visited him before.

reading.ru: Да мы знаем, что тяжело, – пропели ангелы.
reading.question: What does Venichka confess to the angels?
options: That things are hard for him
That he has lost his money
That he has forgotten the way to Petushki
That he no longer believes in them
reading.correct: That things are hard for him
reading.explain: He tells them quietly "Тяжело мне", and the angels answer that they know.

reading.ru: А ты походи, легче будет, а через полчаса магазин откроется: водка там с девяти, правда, а красненького сразу дадут…
reading.question: What do the angels say about the shop that is about to open?
options: Vodka is only sold from nine, but red wine will be given straight away
It will not open until the evening
reading.correct: Vodka is only sold from nine, but red wine will be given straight away
reading.explain: The angels tell him to walk about a little; in half an hour the shop opens, with vodka from nine but red wine at once.

reading.question: How does Venichka react when the angels confirm the red wine will be cold?
reading.explain: After the exchange about the cold red wine he exclaims how excited he has become.

reading.ru: Вы же сами знаете, каково в моем состоянии – ходить!..
reading.question: Why does Venichka object to the angels' advice to walk about?
options: In his condition walking is unbearable
He is afraid of missing the train
He has nowhere to leave his suitcase
reading.correct: In his condition walking is unbearable
reading.explain: He replies that he does not feel like walking and that they themselves know what walking is like in his state.

reading.question: Why do the angels send Venichka into the station restaurant?
options: Because there was sherry there the evening before
Because his friends are waiting there
reading.correct: Because there was sherry there the evening before
reading.explain: They remember the sherry of the previous evening and argue that it cannot all have been drunk in one night.

reading.question: How do the angels answer when Venichka thanks them?
options: They ask him for a present
reading.explain: They sing "На здоровье, Веня…" and then, still more tenderly, "Не стоит…", and he finds them lovely.

reading.ru: В Петушки без гостинцев никак нельзя.
reading.question: What does Venichka say about travelling to Petushki?
options: It is out of the question to go there without presents
It is better to go there in the evening
It is impossible to get there from the Kursk station
One should never go there sober
reading.correct: It is out of the question to go there without presents
reading.explain: He is glad he bought the presents the day before, since one simply cannot go to Petushki without them.

reading.ru: Это ангелы мне напомнили о гостинцах, потому что те, для кого они куплены, сами напоминают ангелов.
reading.question: Why does Venichka think it was the angels who reminded him of the presents?
options: Because the people the presents are for are themselves like angels
Because the angels want the presents for themselves
Because he had left the presents at the shop
Because the angels had helped him choose them
reading.correct: Because the people the presents are for are themselves like angels
reading.explain: He reasons that the ones for whom the gifts were bought resemble angels, so angels naturally brought them to mind.

reading.ru: Я пошел через площадь – вернее, не пошел, а повлекся.
reading.question: How does Venichka describe his crossing of the square?
options: He did not walk so much as drag himself
He was carried by two strangers
He crossed it without stopping once
reading.correct: He did not walk so much as drag himself
reading.explain: He corrects himself: it was not walking but dragging, with two or three halts to quell the sickness.

reading.ru: Так вот, я каждую минуту ждал, что меня, посреди площади, начнет тошнить со всех трех сторон.
reading.question: What did Venichka fear every minute in the middle of the square?
options: Being sick from all three sides of his nature at once
Losing his presents in the crowd
reading.correct: Being sick from all three sides of his nature at once
reading.explain: Having just described man's physical, spiritual and mystical sides, he expects nausea from all three.

reading.ru: Между ними была пауза в тридцать секунд, а я не сверхчеловек, чтобы в тридцать секунд что-нибудь успеть.
reading.question: Why could he not have bought the presents between the two glasses of hunter's vodka?
options: The pause between them lasted only thirty seconds
He had no money left by then
He was not in Moscow at that hour
reading.correct: The pause between them lasted only thirty seconds
reading.explain: He rules the moment out because thirty seconds is not enough time for anyone who is not a superman.

highlight.question: Which sentence quotes what the Redeemer said even to his own Mother?
sentences: – Да брось ты, – отмахнулся я от себя, – разве суета мне твоя нужна?
люди разве твои нужны?
Ведь вот Искупитель даже, и даже Маме своей родной, и то говорил: «Что мне до тебя?»
А уж тем более мне – что мне до этих суетящихся и постылых?
highlight.explain: The third sentence carries the quoted words of the Redeemer to his Mother.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the beings Venichka has just recognised?
sentences: О!
Узнаю!
Это опять они!
Ангелы Господни!
Это вы опять?
highlight.explain: Only the fourth sentence actually names them as the angels of the Lord.

highlight.question: Which sentence repeats back to the angels the advice they have just given him?
sentences: – Вы говорите: походи, походи, легче будет.
Да ведь и ходить-то не хочется…
Вы же сами знаете, каково в моем состоянии – ходить!..
highlight.explain: The first sentence quotes the angels' own words back at them; the other two are his objection.

highlight.question: Which sentence argues that some of the drink from last night must still be left?
sentences: – А ты вот чего: ты зайди в ресторан вокзальный.
Может, там чего и есть.
Там вчера вечером херес был.
Не могли же выпить за вечер весь херес!..
highlight.explain: The last sentence reasons that the whole stock of sherry cannot have been drunk in a single evening.

highlight.question: Which sentence explains why the angels of all beings were the ones to remind him about the presents?
sentences: Какие они милые!..
Ну что ж…
Идти так идти.
И как хорошо, что я вчера гостинцев купил, – не ехать же в Петушки без гостинцев.
В Петушки без гостинцев никак нельзя.
Это ангелы мне напомнили о гостинцах, потому что те, для кого они куплены, сами напоминают ангелов.
Хорошо, что купил…
А когда ты их вчера купил? вспомни… иди и вспоминай…
highlight.explain: The sixth sentence gives the reason: the people the presents are for are themselves like angels.

highlight.question: Which sentence lists the different sides that, according to Venichka, make up a human being?
sentences: Я пошел через площадь – вернее, не пошел, а повлекся.
Два или три раза я останавливался – и застывал на месте, чтобы унять в себе дурноту.
Ведь в человеке не одна только физическая сторона; в нем и духовная сторона есть, и есть – больше того – есть сторона мистическая, сверхдуховная сторона.
Так вот, я каждую минуту ждал, что меня, посреди площади, начнет тошнить со всех трех сторон.
И опять останавливался и застывал.
highlight.explain: The third sentence enumerates the physical, spiritual and mystical sides of a person.
